answer: An agent market requires every active identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days, and each bond permits only ten bids per hour. Agents named lantern, kernel, and falcon follow the same rule: splitting into extra identities grants no free capacity because each needs its own bond. An attacker seeking 10,000 bids per hour must lock 100,000 tokens across 1,000 identities, tying up capital for a month and bearing its financing cost.
